title: movement_indicator_none_test hyphen check is vacuous — matches CSS class hyphens, never fails
detail: string.contains(html, "-") now always passes — the rendered span's classes (text-slate, text-sm) and data-testid both contain hyphens, so the assertion can't detect a missing placeholder.
recommended_fix: Make the assertion content-specific (assert the span's text equals "-"), or restore the em-dash placeholder so the old em-dash check stays meaningful.

title: no_em_dash_test checks the same U+2014 character twice (redundant ||)
detail: Both operands test the identical U+2014 character — the \u{2014} escape and the literal em-dash resolve to the same byte, so the || compares identical booleans (dead duplication).
recommended_fix: Keep a single contains() call — the escape form and the literal are the same character, so one suffices.

title: no_em_dash_test claims a global copy ban but can only reach toast/page strings
evidence:
+/// any landlord-facing copy string. Pins the ban durably so a single
+/// reintroduced dash fails CI instead of shipping.
+            <> " applicants waiting. See who's strongest",
detail: The comment promises coverage of "any landlord-facing copy string," but for_each_copy can only enumerate strings it computes (toast/page results), not inline literals in component modules — so the ban is unenforceable there.
recommended_fix: Either narrow the comment to "all copy.toast/page strings," or add a repo-wide grep/lint guard so an em-dash in any component module also fails CI.
